en: The cool amihan wind blows from the northeast across the Philippines between November and February.
Volcanic ash from Mayon Volcano enriches the local soil with minerals that help abaca plants grow.
Pumice is a highly porous volcanic rock formed from cooled lava that can actually float on water.
Cold morning temperatures in Baguio City cause water vapor in the air to condense into thick fog.
Because the Philippines is near the equator, the Sun appears almost directly overhead at noon.
The bright stars forming the Orion constellation are easily visible in the Philippine night sky during December.
The gravitational pull of the Moon causes the water level in Manila Bay to rise and fall daily.
Strong typhoons push ocean water far inland, causing destructive storm surges in coastal Philippine towns.
The southwest monsoon brings heavy rainfall to the western parts of the Philippines from June to September.
The white sand of Boracay Island is composed primarily of crushed coral and tiny foraminifera shells.
Intense earthquake shaking can cause water-saturated soil in coastal areas to temporarily behave like a liquid.
Heat from the Sun causes liquid water in Laguna de Bay to evaporate into invisible water vapor.
